articles.title: VetBrief: Turning Worried Pet-Owner Stories into Clearer Veterinary Intake Notes
articles.excerpt: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Weekend Challenge: Build for a Friend I built VetBrief, a lightweight veterinary intake and appointment request tool designed to help pet owners communicate…
articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Weekend Challenge: Build for a Friend What I Built I built VetBrief , a lightweight veterinary intake and appointment request tool designed to help pet owners communicate more clearly with veterinary clinics. I built it with a friend and veterinary-clinic context in mind. When people are worried about an animal, they often explain what is happening in a long or unstructured way: “She has been hiding since yesterday, she normally sleeps on the sofa, she did not eat breakfast, and she walked away when I tried to touch her.” All of that information may be useful, but veterinary staff need to identify the key facts quickly. VetBrief helps organise that information before the appointment.

articles.title: Cue: a drum machine whose song is a Sanity dataset
articles.excerpt: This is a submission for the Sanity Challenge, Path One: Ship an Agent That Queries Real Content Cue is a drum machine whose song is a Sanity document. There are no audio files. The browser reads the…
articles.body: This is a submission for the Sanity Challenge, Path One: Ship an Agent That Queries Real Content What I Built Cue is a drum machine whose song is a Sanity document. There are no audio files. The browser reads the numbers in the dataset and plays them as sound. A DJ cues the next track in headphones while the room hears the current one. A Sanity document already has that split: a draft and a published version. Cue makes it literal. The Floor is a public page. It plays the published song, with no token. The Deck is a Sanity App SDK app. It edits the draft and plays it in a Cue channel that only the DJ hears. Drop publishes the draft. Every open Floor switches to the new song on the next bar line. Published is the room. Drafts are the headphones. Publishing is the drop.

articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Weekend Challenge: Build for a Friend ( https://dev.to/challenges/hacktoberfest-weekend-2026-10-01 ) What I Built I built LocalCommit, a lightweight CLI tool that inspects your staged git diffs and drafts concise Conventional Commit messages (feat(auth): add refresh token rotation) running entirely on your local machine using Ollama. I built this for my friend Manish, a software engineer working under strict client non-disclosure agreements. Manish's team requires strict Conventional Commits for automated changelogs and semantic releases, but company policy strictly forbids piping source code or git diffs to proprietary cloud LLM APIs (like OpenAI or Anthropic).

articles.body: Tom Cruise's Digger bombed hard in theaters, pulling in an estimated $20 million in its opening weekend at the global box office. It's a crushing start for the Alejandro González Iñárritu-directed dark comedy. The movie, which stars an unrecognizable Cruise under a thick bed of makeup, accumulated just $8 million domestically and $12 million internationally. It's a $20 million total that props Digger up to be crushed under the weight of its $160 million production budget (via Deadline ). With marketing costs unclear, it signals a long, long line to walk if the movie wants to even sniff at turning a profit. "An oil tycoon faces a mounting environmental catastrophe as politicians and scientists struggle to contain the crisis," a description for Digger says.

articles.body: Credit: SOULOG Plenty of important details get said out loud once and never written down: a price quoted on a call, a delivery date mentioned as a meeting wraps up, the name of a tool a colleague recommends in passing. In a week full of calls, meetings, and classes, most of them are gone by the time you need them. A standard voice recorder certainly helps, but it leaves you with hours of audio and transcripts to dig through, with nothing linking the words to the files, photos, and earlier conversations around them. The Soulog Sense , paired with the Soulog app, not only records and transcribes the conversation but also sorts it by topic and decision and connects it to the surrounding material, so you can search it, revisit it, and build on it later. Here’s what you need to know.

articles.body: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 October 3 –… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. Selfie at Vera Rubin Ridge Explanation: On sol 1943 of its journey of exploration across the surface of Mars, the Curiosity Rover recorded this selfie at the south rim of Vera Rubin Ridge. Of course a sol is a Martian solar day , about 40 minutes longer than an Earth day. Curiosity’s sol 1943 corresponds to Earth date January 23, 2018.

articles.body: NASA astronaut Christina Koch is seen during an event to award the Congressional Space Medal of Honor to the Artemis II crew, Friday, Aug. 28, 2026, at the agency’s Johnson Space Center in Houston. Credit: NASA/John Kraus As part of NASA’s ongoing Inspiration Tour, NASA astronaut Christina Koch will highlight America’s strengths in space exploration and aeronautics innovation at the Philadelphia Eagles vs. Los Angeles Rams game in Philadelphia on Sunday, Oct. 4. A self-proclaimed Philadelphia sports fan, Koch is an explorer and engineer who spent a total of 338 days in space across two missions, including serving as a mission specialist for the agency’s Artemis II mission earlier this year.

articles.excerpt: NASA’s SpaceX Crew-12 mission is ending, with the crew scheduled to return in early October. NASA astronauts Jessica Meir and Jack Hathaway, ESA (European Space Agency) astronaut Sophie Adenot, and Ro…
articles.body: 5 Min Read Heading Home: NASA’s SpaceX Crew-12 Concludes Station Science Mission NASA’s SpaceX Crew-12 mission is ending, with the crew scheduled to return in early October. NASA astronauts Jessica Meir and Jack Hathaway, ESA (European Space Agency) astronaut Sophie Adenot, and Roscosmos cosmonaut Andrey Fedyaev will head home from the International Space Station after supporting research that benefits life on Earth and prepares humans for missions into deep space. Here’s a look back at some of their accomplishments: Orbital transit NASA/ESA The crew members look out the window of a Dragon spacecraft during their journey to the space station, a destination that offers a unique vantage point to observe both Earth and the cosmos.
